the catalytic and regulatory functions, such as heparin affinity, antithrombin-III inactivation, are affected by the modification or oxidation of only one tryptophyl residue of thrombin.

the catalytic and regulatory functions in thrombin.
the identification of residues of thrombin which are essential for its catalytic, regulatory, and binding functions.
the identification of the functional and structural role of the single tryptophyl residue of thrombin.

modification of one trytophan residue in thrombin by N-bromosucinimide results in a decrease of the affinity of the enzyme for heparin and a concomitant decrease in the catalytic activity of the modified enzyme.
modification of a single residue, a tryptophan in thrombin, results in a significant change in the catalytic and regulatory properties of the enzyme.

modification of one trytophan residue of bovine thrombin affects its affinity to heparin, but the structural environment of the tyrosyl groups is not altered significantly.
